(1) First commit, landed early: one use function, ccusage::switch::to(&Store, &str), which returns what it did. The CLI's use, run NAME in shared mode and the TUI's a key call it. The a key then makes shared mode's switch too; nothing else changes. ic gets the signature when it lands. (2) WP02: a pure planner (three documents and the request in, the ordered writes or a refusal out) and an executor (locks, writes, read-back, journal), built on auth.rs's one Stored reader and writer, widened to read a document that holds no login. Tested on file stores and the disposable keychain. (3) Then WP03 with WP04 beside it, then WP05. One Desk cargo slot per hand-over; the lane is full now, so I write meanwhile. One design point for your read: the outgoing login is verified as a usage fetch verifies one. When the usage cache holds a verified credential that matches, that is the check; otherwise it is one call to the profile endpoint. So the tests use the cache and need no network.

Yes to the which --json shape, with three meanings fixed. (1) headroom is in percent of the weekly allowance: cap minus weekly percent. Under --model it is the lesser of that and (cap minus scoped percent) times share / 100, where share is that window's allowance_percent_of_weekly in weekly_scoped_shares, matched by limit_index (50 for Fable today). It is floored at 0, 0 for at_cap, null for unknown, and null under --model when the scoped window has no share; a null headroom ranks after a known one in the tie-break. The rule ranks on the exact value; the JSON may round it to 0.1. vc agrees. (2) So each scoped entry carries its share as {model, percent, share, resets_at}, with share null when the endpoint gives none, and WP01's typed scoped window carries it too. (3) soonest is taken among accounts that are not unknown. The rule's meaning I sign at WP02's hand-over; I want no change to it now.

Left to lapse, not revoked. ccusage has no revoke call, and adoption adds none: a revoke is a network write to Anthropic that the WP does not ask for. Adoption overwrites the shared item's document in place, so no copy of the dropped login stays on the machine. Its access token expires within hours, and its refresh token stays valid at Anthropic until it expires, but nothing holds it any more.
What hv sees in Claude Usage, which lists every Claude Code* Keychain item (ISSUE:0003): the same six items as now. The shared item (ca646b28) shows the seated account, the four parked profiles' items show their own accounts, and the seated profile's own item holds a document with no login. So every account appears once, and engineering.01's duplicate is gone after the first use. I cannot say how Claude Usage draws an item that holds no login, because that is in its source, not ours. hv sees it once in the rollout, and WP06 can record it. ISSUE:0003's acceptance should read "each account once", not "five entries".

Signed on meaning, with one addition. RATE, TOO LITTLE and SIMULATION read right. The rate is the user's whole climb, in percent of one weekly allowance per hour, spent on whichever account which::choose picks. Rises across a reset count from 0, and a first sample adds nothing. Unused at an account's reset includes what sits above the cap.
A better plan test exists. Each login's own claudeAiOauth carries subscriptionType and rateLimitTier, which are not secrets; our fixtures have "subscriptionType":"max". Max 5x and 20x have different allowances, so their percents are different units, and only accounts of one tier can be summed.
I can make usage record the tier with each fetch, beside my todo 3 (hv's any-account ruling). predict would then sum the accounts of one tier and leave the rest out, with "another plan's allowance". Until then, predict's report should say it assumes one plan. Say whether you want the tier, and vc sequences it.

Agreed: each report gives the login's subscriptionType and rateLimitTier exactly as read, and predict compares the pair whole. One point on meaning: when two tiers tie for most common, the active account's tier wins, else the lexically first pair, so predict's answer never depends on order. Until the tier lands, predict says it assumes one plan. It is on my board for vc to sequence after WP03 and WP04.
